ironclad.title: Ironclad Guide — Decks, Playstyle & Strategy
ironclad.overview: The Ironclad is the bruiser of Slay the Spire 2. His cards revolve around HP manipulation, Strength scaling, and Exhaust synergies. Burning Blood heals him after every combat, making him forgiving for newer players while still offering deep build variety.
ironclad.startingRelic: Burning Blood — heals for a small amount at the end of each combat.

strengths.0: Easy to pilot and beginner friendly
strengths.1: Heals after combat via Burning Blood
strengths.3: High damage ceiling with multi-hit attacks

weaknesses.0: Exhaust can be awkward to manage
weaknesses.1: Self-damage builds require careful HP management
weaknesses.2: Relies on setup turns for scaling builds
weaknesses.3: Vulnerable to enemies that remove buffs

0.name: Strength Build
0.desc: Strength remains the Ironclad's primary scaling method. Buff Strength with cheap generators, then leverage multi-hit attacks where each hit benefits from the bonus. Simple to pilot and effective at all Ascension levels.

cardNotes.0: Cheap Strength generator — play early for immediate value
cardNotes.1: Hits twice, each benefiting from Strength
cardNotes.2: Best multi-hit card with AoE — scales with both Strength and Energy
cardNotes.3: Best passive Strength generation, but requires setup turn
cardNotes.4: Multi-hit attack that scales with Strength on each hit
cardNotes.5: Thins your deck of Strikes/Defends and scales with Rupture

relicNotes.0: Free Block on turn 1 — buys time to set up Demon Form
relicNotes.1: Risk/reward — huge Strength but enemies gain some too

tips.0: Multi-hit cards benefit from Strength on each hit — prioritize them over single-hit attacks
tips.1: Vulnerable amplifies high-damage Strength attacks significantly — even one source helps
tips.2: Extra Energy allows you to set up Demon Form and still play cards the same turn
tips.3: In Act 1, take Inflame or any cheap Strength source over expensive scaling like Demon Form

1.name: Block Build
1.desc: Stack Block with Barricade, Stone Armor, and defensive powers, then convert your massive Block into damage with Body Slam. Very safe once online, but slow to set up — prioritize defensive cards early.

cardNotes.0: Core power — Block no longer resets at start of turn
cardNotes.1: Converts your entire Block stack into damage — the win condition
cardNotes.2: Massive single-turn Block — great for surviving big hits
cardNotes.3: Gives Plating for passive Block every turn
cardNotes.4: Solid Block + card draw — always useful

relicNotes.0: Free Block on turn 1 — stacks with Barricade
relicNotes.1: Block on turn 1 — helps survive until setup is complete
relicNotes.2: Adds passive Block generation each turn

tips.0: Barricade is the single most important card — without it, Block resets each turn and the build falls apart
tips.1: Body Slam is your only reliable damage source, so take it early when offered
tips.2: Look for Dexterity sources to scale Block passively alongside your powers
tips.3: This build struggles in Act 1 before you find Barricade — take strong early Attacks to survive

2.name: Exhaust Build
2.desc: Thin your deck mid-combat by Exhausting cards, triggering powerful on-exhaust effects. Corruption makes all Skills free but Exhausts them — pair with Feel No Pain for Block and Dark Embrace for draw. High skill ceiling but devastating when assembled.

cardNotes.0: Makes all Skills cost 0 but Exhausts them — the engine
cardNotes.1: Draw a card whenever you Exhaust — keeps your hand full
cardNotes.2: Gain Block on every Exhaust — your defense while comboing
cardNotes.3: Exhausts entire hand for massive single-target damage
cardNotes.4: Exhausts all non-Attack cards for Block — great with Corruption

relicNotes.0: Deals damage to all enemies whenever you Exhaust a card
relicNotes.1: Post-combat heal offsets any chip damage from aggressive plays

tips.0: Corruption + Dark Embrace is the dream combo — play every Skill for free and draw replacements
tips.1: Feel No Pain is your defense — without it, Exhausting your Skills leaves you vulnerable
tips.2: Don't play Corruption until you have at least one on-exhaust payoff in play
tips.3: Be careful not to Exhaust cards you still need — plan your turn order before playing

3.name: Bloodletting Build
3.desc: Trade HP for power. Self-damage cards like Offering and Bloodletting trigger Rupture for permanent Strength gains. Burning Blood helps offset the HP cost. High risk, high reward — the most aggressive Ironclad archetype.

cardNotes.0: Gains Strength whenever you lose HP from a card — the payoff engine
cardNotes.1: Lose HP to draw 3 and gain Energy — one of the best cards in the game
cardNotes.2: Lose HP to deal high damage — triggers Rupture
cardNotes.3: Lose HP to gain Energy — triggers Rupture and accelerates turns
cardNotes.4: Gain Block whenever you play an Attack — sustain while going aggressive

relicNotes.0: Post-combat heal offsets the self-damage — essential for consistency
relicNotes.1: Bonus Strength when at low HP — synergizes naturally with self-damage

tips.0: Rupture is only worth taking if you have 2+ cards that make you lose HP
tips.1: Offering is always good, even outside this build — never skip it
tips.2: Burning Blood's heal is more valuable here than in any other build
tips.3: Watch your HP — don't play self-damage cards when you can't afford the cost

bossMatchups.0: Strength scaling races the Beast before it buffs. Burst during stun windows. Flame Barrier punishes multi-attacks. Watch for Ringing turns limiting you to 1 card.
bossMatchups.1: Multi-hit attacks like Whirlwind strip Slippery stacks fast. Save Block for Turn 3 Dismember (27 dmg). Burst on Turn 4 safe window.
bossMatchups.2: Use her 3 sleep turns to set up Demon Form or Barricade. Front-load damage once she wakes. She debuffs Strength — Block builds are safer.
bossMatchups.3: Play Beckon cards immediately to avoid unblockable damage. Don’t waste attacks during Intangible phases. Concentrate damage on turns 2-3.
bossMatchups.4: Big HP pool but predictable. Stack Strength and burst with Whirlwind. Save Block for the explosion turn when he dies at 0 HP.
bossMatchups.5: Always face the attacking claw. Kill Rocket first (higher damage), then burst Crusher. Flame Barrier and Shrug It Off are premium.
bossMatchups.6: Play aggressively — Ponder heals 30 HP + Strength. Pick Disintegration if your build is fast. Save Offering for burst turns.
bossMatchups.7: Pure DPS race — Sandpit counter kills you at 0. Always play Frantic Escape cards. Never use random Exhaust (may remove Escapes).
bossMatchups.8: Kill the Amalgam first (before turn 10). Whirlwind clears adds while Strength handles Queen. Plan around Chains locking 3 cards.
bossMatchups.9: Multiple phases — Doormaker HP persists between cycles. Barricade/Body Slam is safest. Burst during the stun turn after Door transforms.

ascensionTips.0: A1-4: Ironclad is forgiving. Take strong Attacks early, rely on Burning Blood healing. Fight Elites for relics.
ascensionTips.1: A5: You start with Ascender's Bane curse. Remove it at the first shop — a dead card in your deck costs you turns.
ascensionTips.2: A6-7: Fewer Rest Sites and rarer upgrades. Strength + Block hybrid is the most consistent. Don't rely on finding specific Rares.
ascensionTips.3: A8-9: Enemies have more HP and deal more damage. Draft defensively — Flame Barrier and Shrug It Off are premium picks.
ascensionTips.4: A10: Double boss at Act 3 end. Barricade/Body Slam is the safest boss-killer. Deck must handle two full fights back-to-back.

0.note: Raw damage and basic defense. Need to kill Elites fast.

1.note: Start building your archetype. Key Powers define the rest of the run.

2.note: Win conditions and boss-killers. Skip anything that doesn't directly support your build.

silent.title: Silent Guide — Decks, Playstyle & Strategy
silent.overview: The Silent uses Poison, Shivs, and discard synergies to control fights. She has excellent card draw and deck cycling, but low base HP (70) makes her fragile. Rewards careful deck construction over raw power.
silent.startingRelic: Ring of the Snake — draw 2 additional cards on the first turn of each combat.

strengths.0: Excellent card draw and deck cycling
strengths.1: Poison scales infinitely against high-HP enemies
strengths.2: Shivs provide burst damage with low commitment
strengths.3: Strong discard synergies for hand manipulation

weaknesses.0: Low base HP (70) makes her fragile
weaknesses.1: Poison is slow against multiple enemies
weaknesses.2: Requires careful deck construction to avoid bloat
weaknesses.3: Shiv builds need Strength scaling to stay relevant

0.name: Poison Build
0.desc: Apply Poison and let it tick enemies down each turn. Noxious Fumes provides passive scaling while Envenom turns every Attack into a Poison applicator. Focus on survival — Poison does the killing for you.

cardNotes.0: Applies Poison to all enemies every turn — set it up early and let it stack
cardNotes.1: Every Attack hit applies Poison — turns Shivs and multi-hits into Poison engines
cardNotes.2: Cheap, reliable Poison application — solid early pick
cardNotes.3: Spreads Poison across multiple enemies — good for AoE fights
cardNotes.4: Retains in hand and applies Poison — consistent value each turn

relicNotes.0: Extra Poison on application — accelerates your Poison stacking
relicNotes.1: Applies Poison to all enemies at combat start — free head start

tips.0: Noxious Fumes is your highest priority card — it scales passively without costing cards or Energy
tips.1: Envenom + Blade Dance is a strong combo: 3 Shivs = 3 Poison applications
tips.2: In multi-enemy fights, focus on surviving — Poison ticks on all enemies simultaneously
tips.3: Don't over-draft Poison cards. 2-3 strong sources plus defense is better than 6 Poison cards and no Block

1.name: Shiv Build
1.desc: Generate 0-cost Shivs and boost them with Accuracy and Strength scaling. Each Shiv played triggers on-attack effects from relics, making quantity more valuable than individual damage.

cardNotes.0: Gives +4 damage to all Shivs — the build-defining card
cardNotes.1: Creates 3 Shivs for 1 Energy — your bread and butter
cardNotes.2: Shivs + Block in one card — offense and defense
cardNotes.3: Generates a free Shiv every turn — passive value
cardNotes.4: Replaces your hand with Shivs — huge burst with Accuracy up

relicNotes.0: Gain Strength every 3 Attacks played — Shivs trigger this fast
relicNotes.1: Gain Dexterity every 3 Attacks played — free Block scaling
relicNotes.2: Gain Block every 3 Attacks played — passive defense from playing Shivs

tips.0: Accuracy is the #1 priority — without it, Shivs deal too little damage to scale
tips.1: Shuriken and Kunai are what make this build viable in late game — seek them out
tips.2: Shivs are Attacks, so any "when you play an Attack" effect triggers on each one
tips.3: This build needs Strength or Accuracy to stay relevant past Act 2 — don't commit without a scaling source

2.name: Discard Build
2.desc: Discard cards to trigger powerful on-discard effects like Reflex and Tactician, generating free cards and Energy. Tools of the Trade filters your hand every turn. The most cycle-heavy Silent archetype.

cardNotes.0: Draw and discard each turn — consistent hand filtering forever
cardNotes.1: Draw 2 cards when discarded — free card advantage
cardNotes.2: Gain Energy when discarded — free resources every cycle
cardNotes.3: Discard entire hand and redraw — triggers all on-discard effects at once
cardNotes.4: Block + discard a card — triggers Reflex/Tactician while defending

relicNotes.0: Gain Block whenever you discard — free defense from your engine
relicNotes.1: Deal damage for each card discarded — turns cycling into damage

tips.0: Reflex and Tactician are the engine — draft them before committing to this archetype
tips.1: Tools of the Trade is the best sustained value card for this build — take it whenever offered
tips.2: Calculated Gamble + multiple Reflex/Tactician = explosive turns with huge card and Energy generation
tips.3: This build needs a separate damage source — discard effects alone won't kill bosses

bossMatchups.0: Poison scales well against 252 HP. Use stun windows for setup. Ringing (1 card/turn) is brutal — Wraith Form or Noxious Fumes carry through.
bossMatchups.1: Shivs strip Slippery stacks fast. Save all Block for Turn 3 Dismember (27 dmg + Wounds). Silent's low HP makes Dismember lethal without Block.
bossMatchups.2: Sustained damage is dangerous with 70 HP. Use sleep turns to set up Noxious Fumes and Wraith Form. Poison ignores her Strength debuffs.
bossMatchups.3: Play Beckon cards immediately. Don't attack during Intangible phases. Poison ticks ignore Intangible — Noxious Fumes is perfect here.
bossMatchups.4: Poison stacks tick reliably against 250 HP. Save Block for the explosion turn. Apply Weak before killing to reduce explosion damage.
bossMatchups.5: Big hits devastate Silent's low HP. Footwork and Leg Sweep are must-haves. Face the attacking claw. Kill Rocket first.
bossMatchups.6: Play aggressively — don't let Ponder heal 30 HP. Poison ignores enemy buffs. Malaise shuts down big attack turns. Pick Disintegration over Mind Rot.
bossMatchups.7: Poison is perfect for this DPS race. Always play Frantic Escape cards. Catalyst doubles Poison for a quick kill before Sandpit reaches 0.
bossMatchups.8: Envenom + Blade Dance poisons everything. Noxious Fumes ticks on Queen + Amalgam. Kill Amalgam first — Silent excels in multi-target fights.
bossMatchups.9: Poison persists between Doormaker phases — ideal for Silent. Catalyst doubles Poison for lethal burst. After Image provides sustain across cycles.

ascensionTips.0: A1-4: Poison is reliable and forgiving. Take Deadly Poison and Noxious Fumes. Card draw is king — Backflip and Acrobatics.
ascensionTips.1: A5: Ascender's Bane hurts your thin deck. Remove it ASAP or draft more card draw to compensate for the dead card.
ascensionTips.2: A6-7: Low HP with fewer Rest Sites is punishing. Footwork is now a must-draft card. Defensive picks > damage picks.
ascensionTips.3: A8-9: Enemies have more HP and damage. Wraith Form becomes essential for boss fights. Poison is more consistent than Shivs here.
ascensionTips.4: A10: Double boss demands a deck that can handle two full fights. Catalyst + Burst is the fastest boss kill. Keep decks to 15-17 cards.

0.note: Cheap damage and early defense. Silent is fragile — don't take unnecessary damage.

1.note: Commit to Poison or Shivs. Take the scaling card that matches your current draft.

2.note: Boss-killing finishers and sustain. Catalyst doubles Poison for lethal burst.

defect.title: Defect Guide — Decks, Playstyle & Strategy
defect.overview: The Defect channels Orbs — Lightning, Frost, Dark, and Plasma — that trigger passively each turn and on evoke. Focus increases all Orb output. Complex to learn but scales hard once you understand Orb management.
defect.startingRelic: Cracked Core — channel 1 Lightning Orb at the start of each combat.

strengths.0: Orbs provide passive damage and block every turn
strengths.1: Focus scaling multiplies all Orb output
strengths.2: Frost Orbs generate block passively each turn

weaknesses.0: Complex mechanics have a steep learning curve
weaknesses.1: Requires setup turns to get Orbs online
weaknesses.2: Limited Orb slots can bottleneck scaling
weaknesses.3: Mixing too many Orb types dilutes the strategy

0.name: Frost Focus Build
0.desc: Channel Frost Orbs and stack Focus to generate massive passive Block every turn. Once online, most enemies simply can't break through your defense. The most consistent Defect archetype.

cardNotes.0: Channels 2 Frost Orbs and gives Block — the build's best card
cardNotes.1: Permanent Focus — multiplies all Orb output for the rest of combat
cardNotes.2: Huge Focus burst but loses 1 per turn — win fast or find Artifact
cardNotes.3: Channels Frost and draws a card — efficient early pick
cardNotes.4: Deals damage based on Frost Orbs channeled — your finisher

relicNotes.0: Extra Orb slots — more Orbs = more passive Block per turn
relicNotes.1: Free Focus — directly multiplies your Frost Block generation
relicNotes.2: Starting relic channels Lightning turn 1 — helps early before Frost is online

tips.0: Focus is multiplicative — 3 Focus with 4 Frost Orbs = 12 extra Block per turn passively
tips.1: Biased Cognition is best played when you can win within 3-4 turns or have Artifact to negate the Focus loss
tips.2: More Orb slots is critical — each additional Frost Orb is another source of passive Block
tips.3: This build is weak in Act 1 before you find Focus and Frost cards — draft some early damage

1.name: Lightning Build
1.desc: Channel Lightning Orbs for passive and evoke damage each turn. Storm channels Lightning whenever you play a Power, and Thunder adds passive damage. More aggressive than Frost but less defensive — requires balancing offense with survival.

cardNotes.0: Channels Lightning every time you play a Power — snowballs with more Powers
cardNotes.1: Adds passive Lightning damage each turn — scales with Focus
cardNotes.2: Cheap Attack that channels Lightning — good early pickup
cardNotes.3: Channels Lightning equal to Energy spent — big turn with extra Energy
cardNotes.4: Deals Lightning damage at start of each turn — consistent chip damage

relicNotes.0: Boosts rightmost Orb passive — stronger Lightning ticks
relicNotes.1: Free Focus at combat start — multiplies all Lightning damage

tips.0: Storm + any Power-heavy deck generates Lightning Orbs for free every turn
tips.1: Lightning damage is random — it hits a random enemy, which is great for AoE fights
tips.2: Don't neglect Block — Lightning builds deal good damage but can be fragile without Frost support
tips.3: Tempest is strongest with extra Energy sources — look for Energy relics and cards

2.name: Dark Orb Build
2.desc: Dark Orbs store damage each turn, growing stronger the longer they sit in your Orb slots. Evoke them at the right moment for devastating single-target burst. The highest damage ceiling of any Defect build.

cardNotes.0: Channels Dark Orbs — your primary Dark Orb source
cardNotes.1: Channels a Dark Orb and boosts existing Dark Orbs
cardNotes.2: Evokes rightmost Orb multiple times — massive burst with a charged Dark Orb
cardNotes.3: Triggers first Orb's passive twice per turn — doubles Dark Orb damage gain

relicNotes.0: Free Focus — directly increases Dark Orb damage gain per turn
relicNotes.1: Triggers Orb passives when you take damage — extra Dark Orb charging

tips.0: Dark Orbs deal damage equal to their stored value when evoked — patience is rewarded
tips.1: Multi Cast + a fully charged Dark Orb = hundreds of damage in one turn
tips.2: Focus boosts how much damage Dark Orbs gain passively each turn — prioritize it
tips.3: Mix in some Frost Orbs for defense while your Dark Orbs charge up

bossMatchups.0: Frost Orbs wall the Beast's Plow attacks. Burst during stun windows with Lightning. Ringing (1 card/turn) is manageable with Orb passives doing work for free.
bossMatchups.1: Lightning Orbs help strip Slippery stacks passively. Stack Frost for Turn 3 Dismember block. Claw builds cycle fast enough to strip Slippery quickly.
bossMatchups.2: Use 3 sleep turns to set up Focus and Powers. Frost Orbs trivialize her sustained damage. Lightning races her down before debuffs matter.
bossMatchups.3: Orbs deal passive damage even during Intangible phases (each Orb triggers separately). Frost Focus walls the Scream + Vulnerable turns.
bossMatchups.4: Lightning Orbs chip away at 250 HP passively. Frost Focus makes you nearly invincible. Save Block for the explosion turn at 0 HP.
bossMatchups.5: Big hits bypass Frost partially. Stack high Focus. Kill Rocket first — Lightning Orbs randomly hit both targets. Buffer absorbs Laser attacks.
bossMatchups.6: Debuffs reduce Focus effectiveness. Biased Cognition timing is critical — win fast. Play aggressively to stop Ponder healing 30 HP.
bossMatchups.7: Lightning + Focus provides the DPS needed for this race. Always play Frantic Escape cards. Frost buys time as Sandpit ticks down.
bossMatchups.8: Lightning randomly hits Queen + Amalgam — good for chip damage. Kill Amalgam first. Frost Focus walls survive multi-target pressure. Echo Form is premium.
bossMatchups.9: Orbs scale across phases. Dark Orbs charge up massive damage between Door/Doormaker transitions. Creative AI generates infinite value in long fights.

ascensionTips.0: A1-4: Frost Focus is easy to pilot. Take Glacier and Defragment over everything else. Orbs scale passively.
ascensionTips.1: A5: Ascender's Bane dilutes your deck. Defect needs consistency to draw Focus cards — remove the Bane early.
ascensionTips.2: A6-7: Pure Lightning starts to struggle with fewer Rest Sites. Hybrid Frost+Lightning with Focus is safest.
ascensionTips.3: A8-9: Enemies have more HP — Biased Cognition is riskier without Artifact. Echo Form doubles key plays to compensate.
ascensionTips.4: A10: Double boss needs sustainable scaling. Frost Focus + Capacitor for extra Orb slots handles two full fights consistently.

0.note: Early Orb generators and card draw. You need to survive while Orbs ramp up.

1.note: Core scaling cards. Defragment is the single most important card for any Orb build.

2.note: Power multipliers and Orb slot expansion. Echo Form doubles your best card each turn.

necrobinder.title: Necrobinder Guide — Decks, Playstyle & Strategy
necrobinder.overview: The Necrobinder summons allies and binds souls for persistent effects. Summons attack and block on your behalf each turn. Managing your board state is key — AoE enemies and summon limits create real decision points.
necrobinder.startingRelic: Phylactery Unbound — summon 5 at the start of combat and 2 at the start of each turn.

strengths.0: Summons provide extra damage and block
strengths.1: Soul Binding creates powerful persistent effects
strengths.2: Good at managing multiple threats simultaneously
strengths.3: Unique sacrifice mechanics offer strategic depth

weaknesses.0: Summons can be killed by enemies
weaknesses.3: Can struggle without key summoning cards

0.name: Summon Swarm
0.desc: Fill your board with summons that deal damage and block for you each turn. Every summon is a body that absorbs hits, deals chip damage, or provides Block. Prioritize cards that summon efficiently and protect your board.

cardNotes.0: Core summoning card — fills your board quickly
cardNotes.1: Deals damage AND summons — two effects in one card
cardNotes.2: Summons for all players — massive board presence
cardNotes.4: Basic summon — reliable early game board presence
cardNotes.5: Attack that applies Doom and summons — flexible early pick

relicNotes.0: Starting relic — free summons every combat and every turn
relicNotes.1: Extra Energy turn 1 — lets you summon and play cards immediately

tips.0: Summons provide value every single turn they survive — protecting them is more important than playing new ones
tips.1: AoE enemy attacks can wipe your board — scout enemy intents and save Block for those turns
tips.2: Cards that summon AND do something else (like Sculpting Strike) are the highest priority picks
tips.3: Don't over-commit to summoning without a way to defend your board or yourself

1.name: Soul Binding
1.desc: Bind souls for ongoing passive effects that stack up over time. Each bound soul adds persistent value that compounds across the fight. A control-oriented approach that excels in longer encounters.

cardNotes.0: Binds a soul for a persistent passive effect — core mechanic
cardNotes.1: Power that applies soul-binding effects passively
cardNotes.2: Deals damage based on bound souls — your scaling finisher
cardNotes.3: Versatile card that helps set up your board state
cardNotes.4: Early damage that also contributes to soul effects
cardNotes.5: Damage + summon — supports your board while building souls

relicNotes.0: Free summons each turn — provides board presence while you invest in souls
relicNotes.1: Soul-related relic that accelerates your passive scaling

tips.0: Bound souls stack — each additional soul adds another layer of passive value that compounds
tips.1: This build rewards patience — don't rush damage, let your passives accumulate
tips.2: Soul Storm scales with your bound soul count — it's your primary win condition in long fights
tips.3: Balance soul investment with board defense — dying with 10 bound souls still loses the fight

2.name: Doom Build
2.desc: Apply Doom stacks to enemies, then detonate with Time's Up for massive burst damage. Countdown and Reaper Form accelerate the ticking clock. A unique damage-over-time approach that excels against high-HP bosses.

cardNotes.0: Applies Doom that ticks each turn — your primary Doom source
cardNotes.1: Passively accelerates Doom application every turn — the engine
cardNotes.2: Deals damage equal to enemy's Doom — your burst finisher
cardNotes.3: Applies Doom to ALL enemies — devastating in multi-enemy fights
cardNotes.4: Power that enhances Doom application and scaling
cardNotes.5: Provides defense while your Doom stacks tick down

relicNotes.0: Free summons provide board presence while you wait for Doom to resolve
relicNotes.1: Extra Energy turn 1 — set up Countdown or Reaper Form faster

tips.0: Doom ticks down each turn — stack it high and survive until it resolves for lethal damage
tips.1: Time's Up is your burst finisher — save it for when Doom stacks are high for maximum impact
tips.2: Reaper Form is best played early — the sooner it's active, the more Doom it generates
tips.3: End of Days + Time's Up in multi-enemy fights can clear entire encounters in one combo

bossMatchups.0: Ringing (1 card/turn) is tough but summons still attack. Burst during stun windows. Re-summon aggressively — the Beast's Strength scaling kills boards over time.
bossMatchups.1: Summons help strip Slippery stacks. Save Block and Shared Fate for Turn 3 Dismember (27 dmg). Your board absorbs hits between danger turns.
bossMatchups.2: Use sleep turns to set up summons and Soul Binding. She debuffs Strength — Soul/Doom builds ignore that. Shared Fate protects key summons.
bossMatchups.3: Summons attack during Intangible phases (each hit counts separately). Play Beckon cards immediately. Board presence makes this fight easy.
bossMatchups.4: Summons chip away at 250 HP reliably. Doom ticks effectively against the big HP pool. Board presence wins this war of attrition.
bossMatchups.5: Big single hits kill key summons. Protect with Shared Fate or accept losses. Kill Rocket first — its Laser deals 31 damage.
bossMatchups.6: Play aggressively — Ponder heals 30 HP. Doom build sustains through debuffs. Pick Disintegration over Mind Rot (keep card draw for summons).
bossMatchups.7: DPS race — summons provide extra damage each turn. Always play Frantic Escape cards. Never use random Exhaust effects. Doom ticks help the race.
bossMatchups.8: Your summons vs their Amalgam. Necrobinder wins the war of attrition. Kill Amalgam first. End of Days with Doom wipes everything.
bossMatchups.9: Re-summon between Door/Doormaker phases. Soul Storm is reliable across transitions. Burst the Doormaker during its stun turn each cycle.

ascensionTips.0: A1-4: Summon Swarm is strong and forgiving. Take any summoning card and let your board do the work.
ascensionTips.1: A5: Ascender's Bane is an extra card that can't be played — it dilutes your hand. Remove it fast or draft more card draw.
ascensionTips.2: A6-7: Fewer Rest Sites and rarer cards. Enemies hit harder — summons die faster. Add Shared Fate and Protector for board protection.
ascensionTips.3: A8-9: Enemies have more HP and damage. Soul Binding becomes more reliable than pure summoning — passive scaling survives AoE better.
ascensionTips.4: A10: Double boss at Act 3 end. Doom build with Reaper Form has the highest ceiling. Need tight decks (15-18 cards) to find Time's Up.

0.note: Board presence and early damage. Every summon counts in Act 1 fights.

1.note: Key archetype cards. Commit to Summon, Soul, or Doom based on offerings.

2.note: Win conditions. These cards end boss fights. Skip everything else.

regent.title: Regent Guide — Decks, Playstyle & Strategy
regent.overview: The Regent uses a dual-resource system: Energy and Stars. Star-cost cards are powerful but require dedicated generation. The newest character in StS2, with a flexible playstyle that rewards good resource management.
regent.startingRelic: Ring of the Drake — draw 2 additional cards at the start of your first 3 turns.

strengths.1: Star cards have high impact per play
strengths.3: Good balance of offense and defense

weaknesses.1: Star cards are useless without Stars

0.name: Star Engine
0.desc: Build around Star generation and spend them on high-impact Star-cost cards. The core Regent playstyle. The key rule: always draft Star generators before Star consumers — a hand full of Star cards with no Stars is a dead hand.

cardNotes.0: Core Star generator — reliable income every time you play it
cardNotes.1: Basic attack that generates Stars — your bread and butter
cardNotes.2: Powerful Star-cost payoff card — high damage for Star investment
cardNotes.3: Scaling damage that benefits from Star spending
cardNotes.5: Cheap attack with Star synergy — good early game

relicNotes.0: Starting relic — extra card draw helps find Star generators early
relicNotes.1: Block whenever you create Colorless cards — passive defense

tips.0: Star generation is your #1 priority in Act 1 — take Venerate and Falling Star over flashy Star consumers
tips.1: A good ratio is roughly 2 Star generators for every 1 Star consumer in your deck
tips.2: Don't draft expensive Star cards without the income to support them — bricked hands lose runs
tips.3: Genesis (gain Stars each turn) is the best late-game Star engine if offered — always take it

1.name: Command Build
1.desc: Play a balanced midrange game using the Regent's buff and command cards. Less Star-dependent than Star Engine, making it more consistent when Star generation offerings are weak. Powers provide sustained value over multiple turns.

cardNotes.0: Gain Strength whenever you play a Colorless card — snowballs with card generation
cardNotes.1: Powers up Sovereign Blade permanently — sustained scaling
cardNotes.2: Passive Forge each turn — compounding value the longer the fight lasts
cardNotes.3: Star generation + general utility — always useful
cardNotes.4: Basic attack with Star gen — solid in any Regent deck
cardNotes.5: Reliable mid-range attack — works with or without Stars

relicNotes.0: Extra draw helps find your Powers and setup cards faster
relicNotes.1: Summons a Mini Regent that provides ongoing value

tips.0: Play Powers early — Arsenal, Furnace, and Sword Sage all compound value over time
tips.1: Arsenal + Spectrum Shift (creates Colorless cards each turn) is a strong combo for Strength scaling
tips.2: This build is your fallback when Star offerings are poor — it works with mostly Energy-cost cards
tips.3: Keep some basic Block cards — the Regent lacks innate tankiness without dedicated defense

2.name: Forge Build
2.desc: Forge your Sovereign Blade into a devastating weapon. Stack Forge points to increase its damage, then use Seeking Edge to make it hit all enemies. The Regent's most unique build — all-in on a single powerful card.

cardNotes.0: Permanently increases Sovereign Blade cost and damage — core scaling
cardNotes.1: Makes Sovereign Blade hit ALL enemies and adds Forge — build-defining
cardNotes.2: Passive Forge each turn — set up early for compounding Blade damage
cardNotes.3: Pulls Sovereign Blade from anywhere in your deck — guarantees access
cardNotes.4: Cheap Forge + Energy next turn — efficient early forging
cardNotes.5: Forge + Sovereign Blade deals double damage this turn — burst combo

relicNotes.0: Extra draw helps find Sovereign Blade and Forge cards faster
relicNotes.1: Block on Colorless card creation — passive defense while forging

tips.0: Sovereign Blade is your entire win condition — use Summon Forth to guarantee you draw it each fight
tips.1: Seeking Edge is the most impactful card for this build — it turns Sovereign Blade into AoE
tips.2: Furnace is best played as early as possible — each turn it's active adds more Forge
tips.3: Conqueror + a heavily Forged Sovereign Blade = double damage burst that can one-shot most enemies

bossMatchups.0: Star Engine races the Beast before Strength scaling gets out of control. Burst during stun windows. Forge build with Furnace is safer for sustained fights.
bossMatchups.1: Multi-hit Star cards strip Slippery fast. Save Block and Stars for Turn 3 Dismember. Burst on Turn 4 safe window with Sovereign Blade.
bossMatchups.2: Use sleep turns to set up Furnace and Powers. She debuffs Strength but Forge is permanent — Forge build ignores her debuffs.
bossMatchups.3: Play Beckon cards immediately. Don't attack during Intangible phases. Star Engine provides burst on safe turns.
bossMatchups.4: Star Engine bursts through 250 HP. Sovereign Blade + Seeking Edge handles this cleanly. Save Block for explosion turn.
bossMatchups.5: Big hits need solid defense. Neutron Aegis and Bulwark provide Block. Kill Rocket first. Forge build races Crusher with scaling.
bossMatchups.6: Play aggressively — Ponder heals 30 HP + Strength. Arsenal + Powers scale through debuff choices. Pick Disintegration if your build is fast.
bossMatchups.7: Star Engine's burst damage excels in this DPS race. Always play Frantic Escape cards. Conqueror + Forged Blade can one-shot the Insatiable.
bossMatchups.8: Seeking Edge turns Sovereign Blade into AoE that clears Amalgam + Queen. Kill Amalgam first. Seven Stars hits hard for adds.
bossMatchups.9: Long fight drains Star reserves. Forge build with Furnace + Arsenal scales across phases. Save Conqueror burst for Doormaker stun turns.

ascensionTips.0: A1-4: Star Engine is straightforward and effective. Take Venerate and Falling Star liberally. Fight Elites for relics.
ascensionTips.1: A5: Ascender's Bane dilutes your hand. Regent needs to find Star generators consistently — remove the Bane early at shops.
ascensionTips.2: A6-7: Fewer Rest Sites and rarer cards. Don't over-draft expensive Star consumers without Star income to support them.
ascensionTips.3: A8-9: Enemies have more HP and damage. Forge build with Furnace is the safest scaling — Forge persists and compounds. Bulwark provides reliable Block.
ascensionTips.4: A10: Double boss at Act 3 end. Forge build with Seeking Edge has the highest ceiling — one massive Blade handles both fights. Keep decks to 16-18 cards.

0.note: Star generation and basic damage. Don't take Star consumers without income yet.

1.note: Commit to Star Engine, Command, or Forge. Take the archetype card that matches your draft.

2.note: Build-defining finishers. Seeking Edge makes Forge build unbeatable. Void Form scales Star Engine.

beginner-tips.title: Beginner Tips
beginner-tips.description: Core concepts every new Slay the Spire 2 player should know — card removal, energy management, relic priorities and how to read fights before they happen.

0.heading: Skip More Cards Than You Think
0.text: In Slay the Spire 2, skipping cards is often the right play. A lean deck draws key cards more consistently than a bloated one.

1.heading: Prioritize Card Removal
1.text: Remove Strikes first, then Defends. Your character-specific cards are almost always better.

2.heading: Front-load Your Damage
2.text: Act 1 enemies hit hard and fast. Take strong Attack cards early, transition to scaling in Act 2.

3.heading: Learn Enemy Patterns
3.text: Enemies telegraph their moves with intents. Learn the patterns to optimize your block timing.

4.heading: Potions Are Free Power
4.text: Don't hoard potions. Using them to take 0 damage in a fight is better than saving them "for later".

5.heading: Elite Fights Are Worth It
5.text: Elites give relics which are permanent upgrades. Fight as many as your HP allows.

advanced-strategy.title: Advanced Strategy
advanced-strategy.description: Advanced StS2 strategy: deck pivoting, energy curves, scaling vs burst archetypes, and turn-skip plays for higher Ascensions.

0.heading: Deck Archetypes Over Individual Cards
0.text: A mediocre card that fits your archetype is better than a great card that doesn't. Synergy beats raw power.

1.heading: Damage vs. Scaling
1.text: Act 1: raw damage. Act 2: start scaling. Act 3+: pure scaling wins. Adapt your drafting priorities.

2.heading: Path Planning
2.text: Plan your path through each act before starting. Consider your HP, deck strength, and whether you need shops, campfires, or elites.

3.heading: Energy Management
3.text: Cards that generate energy (or cost 0) are high priority. An extra energy per turn is roughly +25% more plays.

4.heading: Know When to Upgrade vs. Rest
4.text: Upgrading a key card is usually better than healing. Key upgrades can prevent more damage than the heal restores.

5.heading: Boss Relic Swaps
5.text: Trading your starting relic for a boss relic at the start is high risk, high reward. Evaluate based on which character you're playing.

ascension-guide.title: Ascension Guide
ascension-guide.description: All 10 Slay the Spire 2 Ascension levels explained — what changes at each tier, how to adapt your deck, and the right relic and rest-site decisions to climb.

0.heading: How Ascension Works
0.text: Ascension unlocks after beating Act 3. There are 10 levels, tracked per character. All modifiers are cumulative — Ascension 10 has ALL effects active at once.

1.heading: A1: Swarming Elites
1.text: ~60% more Elites spawn on the map. Fight them — relics are permanent power. But plan your HP carefully, more Elites means more damage taken.

2.heading: A2: Weary Traveler
2.text: Healing is reduced to 80% effectiveness. Rest Sites and potions heal less. This makes taking unnecessary damage even more punishing.

3.heading: A3: Poverty
3.text: Enemies and chests drop 25% less Gold. Fewer shop visits, fewer card removals. Prioritize which purchases matter most.

4.heading: A4: Tight Belt
4.text: 1 fewer potion slot. Potions are free power — losing a slot hurts. Use potions aggressively instead of hoarding them.

5.heading: A5: Ascender's Bane
5.text: You start with an unplayable curse card. It dilutes your deck and hand. Remove it at the first shop — a dead card costs you turns every fight.

6.heading: A6-7: Fewer Resources
6.text: A6 removes a Rest Site per Act (fewer heals/upgrades). A7 halves Rare and Upgraded card appearances. Draft more flexibly — you can't rely on finding specific Rares.

7.heading: A8-9: Tougher Enemies
7.text: A8 gives all enemies more HP. A9 makes all enemies deal more damage. Together these make every fight significantly harder. Draft more defensively and keep decks tight.

8.heading: A10: Double Boss
8.text: You fight TWO bosses at the end of Act 3, back to back. Your deck must handle two full HP bars without resting. This is the ultimate test — build for consistency over glass-cannon burst.

9.heading: General High-Ascension Tips
9.text: Skip cards aggressively (15-20 card decks). Remove Strikes first. Fight Elites for relics. Use potions on Elites, not bosses. Upgrade key cards over healing. Don't force builds — adapt to what's offered.
